title: Ingress Shield: two-stage validator and quarantine flow for Console usage events
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Build a robust, low-latency ingestion guardrail (Ingress Shield) for Console usage events that performs a fast edge validation and an async deep schema validation. The goal is to reduce bad events arriving downstream, provide clear observability for validation failures, and quarantine ambiguous/invalid events for investigation and repair without blocking valid traffic. The service should be deployable in the Console backend (Go service) and integrate with the existing events pipeline (Kafka topic events.inbound.console -> transformations -> warehouse).
scope:
- Lightweight synchronous validation at the edge: required top-level fields, timestamp sanity, event type whitelist, small size check.
- Asynchronous deep validation: JSON Schema v4 validation, allowed fields, type coercions, and cross-field consistency checks run in worker pool.
- Quarantine storage for invalid/ambiguous events (S3 prefix + metadata in Postgres).
- Metrics and tracing: ingress.total, ingress.accepted, ingress.rejected, ingress.quarantined, validation.latency_ms, validation.failure_reason counts.
- Dashboard and alerting for spikes in rejection rate and new failure reasons.
- Backwards compatibility: legacy-version compatibility mode and dynamic schema version routing.
- Migration: phased rollout with canary traffic, fallback to legacy topic on increase in latency or error budget breaches.
acceptance_criteria: Edge validation rejects malformed payloads under 3ms p95
Deep validation worker processes 5000 events/s per instance with controlled backpressure
Rejected events land in S3 with a small JSON metadata record and an entry in quarantine table (queryable)
Dashboards surface top 10 failure reasons and allow drilling to example event IDs
Canary rollout to 5% of console traffic and automated rollback if rejection rate > 0.5% compared to baseline
End-to-end test harness that can inject bad and borderline events and assert outcomes
implementation_notes: Design decisions: use JSON Schema for deep validation to keep schemas human-readable and versionable. Edge validator will use a trimmed schema (fast checks) implemented as generated Go structs + hand-written sanity checks to avoid heavy reflection. Use a small in-memory LRU cache for recent schema versions and allow hot-reload via config endpoint. Quarantine format: compressed NDJSON files in s3://redwood-console-quarantine/YYYY/MM/DD/{topic}/{shard}.ndjson with metadata row in postgres.quarantine_events. Use Kafka topic events.inbound.console.valid for accepted events and events.inbound.console.invalid for immediate, non-quarantined rejects. Deep-invalid events go to quarantine and an events.quarantine.notification feed (kafka) consumed by the ops UI.
tradeoffs_and_risks:
- JSON Schema provides flexibility but can be slow for deep validation; mitigated by async workers.
- Quarantining increases storage and operational overhead; reduces downstream poison pills.
- Strict edge validation may accidentally block some unusual but valid client events; mitigate with a permissive canary and compatibility mode.
- Implementation in Go favors existing console backend stack but requires careful memory management for validation libraries.
rollout_plan: 1) Deploy Ingress Shield as read-only mode to canary cluster, emitting metrics but not blocking (2 weeks). 2) Enable blocking for canary (5% traffic) and monitor for 48h. 3) Gradual increase to 25% then 100% with 24h observability windows and automatic rollback if error budget breached. 4) Run a migration window to reprocess quarantine for schema fixes and resume downstream consumption.
monitoring_and_alerts:
- Alert if ingress.rejected_rate > 0.2% sustained for 30m.
- Alert if validation.latency_ms p95 increases > 10% vs baseline.
- Pager on quarantine queue backlog > 10k events older than 6h.
- Dashboard: realtime stream of failure reasons and sample event payloads (obfuscated).
testing_plan: Unit tests for edge checks and schema loader, integration tests with local kafka and s3 emulator, load test to validate worker throughput, chaos test injecting slow schema registry responses, canary smoke tests that assert no increased user-facing latency.
